name: "The Sunbeam II" EP: an interactive short album
author: It_Snow
description:
Retrrofuturistic piano pop in a zine-quality video game—

You are 8 years old again, and you’re scrambling boulders at the seashore. High above you, clouds part and bolts of sun race across the grassy hills.

Or maybe, you’re away from your lover, thinking of the similarities between lost love and found love.

Looking again, you’re middle age, researching ways an ancient civilization foraged medicines. Looking yet again, you’re putting your only child into Hypersleep, just before you send him to another planet, the last time you’ll see him.

Most of all, you’re re-learning, among the boulders, to listen deeply and look closely.

Each action you take mixes and remixes the EP a little bit— will it be heartfelt anthems, or dreamy, braided ear candy? You will choose how to soundtrack your moment.

IMPORTANT: phone controls are minimal at best— all the music is available, but the full interactive experience is best on a laptop or desktop.  

Phone users— if you have notifications silenced, it may also silence the game, so un-silence!

Arrow keys move your player.

B and the potion button change both gravity (temporarily) and sound (more permanently).

If you gather the grasses, they change the sound of the music as well. 

This game should work

Thanks to DH for improvised bassoon— electroacoustic!  Thank you to CL for being our designated “android” friend and for testing. you to Thanks CM for being an early listener, and later for excellent mixing and arranging advice. Thanks to LGB for singing a verse, for time to play, space to be messy, and for the suppert to “go and do music for awhile” each week.  Thanks to AB and LB for years of lessons and listening even when it wasn’t pretty. 

The title song, “Sunbeam II,” honors A.R. Ammons’ “I broke a sheaf of light.”
